articleTitle: An Analytical Model to Determine the Required Charge Near Zero Crossings for Zero Voltage Switching on Single-Stage Isolated Three Phase AC/DC Series Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The single-stage isolated three phase AC to DC series resonant converter with optimal trajectory control technique ensures zero voltage switching for all switching events. Zero voltage switching can be achieved through the utilization of resonant current to charge or discharge parasitic and parallel capacitances of the switching node. However, near zero crossings of the resonant current, the resonant current may not be sufficient to completely charge or discharge the parasitic and parallel capacitances. In this research, an analytical model is presented and experimentally verified to determine the required charge near zero crossings for zero voltage switching in the single-stage isolated three phase AC to DC series resonant converter.

articleTitle: Planning and Operation of Industrial DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper describes best practices and validated approaches for low-voltage industrial DC grids in the fields of electrical planning, control, operation and short and long-term energy management. The lead control approach - the droop curve of the DC bus voltage - is analysed in detail through grid stability. Furthermore, to maintain the desired energy management targets, various approaches to the adaptation of the droop curve are discussed. Validation is based on a large DC grid implemented in the industrial production plant, whereas the gap between modelling results and practical, applicable approaches has been analysed, and possible solutions are proposed.

articleTitle: A Method for Mitigating In-Rush Current of Input Capacitor in DC Distribution Networks through Pre-Charging Capacitor Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper introduces methodology to address the impact of parasitic elements on transmission lines within a direct current distribution network during circuit breaker operations. The proposed technique involves the utilization of pre-charging capacitors as a means to minimize the adverse effects of these parasitic elements. To validate the effectiveness of proposed design method, a comprehensive theoretical analysis, including and simulations, was conducted.

articleTitle: Energy-Equivalent Inductance Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In extensive DC grids and during DC charging of electric vehicles, line and filter inductances play a crucial role in the design of switching elements. The inductively stored energy significantly influences the energy dissipated in the switching elements during the switching process. Therefore, a measurement system for the energy-equivalent inductance is required. This paper presents a novel measurement principle and a measurement system based on it. Laboratory measurements demonstrate that the proposed measurement system provides accurate and reliable results, enabling precise estimation of the energy dissipation in switching elements and facilitating the selection of appropriate switching components.

articleTitle: Unlocking Untapped Solar PV Energy in DC Microgrids Through Hydrogen Energy Storage Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Standalone power systems deployed in regions with challenging grid connectivity often rely on Diesel generators (DGs) for their operation. As a solution to the high operational costs and environmental degradation associated with continuous DG operation, Renewable Energy systems (RES) have emerged as a cost-effective, and environmentally friendly alternative. Integrating RES into standalone power systems demands thorough modelling due to their inherently intermittent nature. Among the solutions that have emerged for the seamless integration of RES into standalone power systems, DC microgrids equipped with energy storage systems have gained prominence. Particularly in critical facilities where power reliability is important, designing of DC microgrids for standalone systems needs a careful consideration of RES's seasonal behaviour. This study focuses on quantifying the untapped energy within solar PV-based DC microgrids, attributable to fluctuations in solar irradiance resulting from seasonal changes. Furthermore, the study assesses the viability of Hydrogen Energy storage as a long-term energy storage solution to harness this untapped energy. The findings underscore that over 50% of potential energy yield from solar PV-based DC microgrids remains untapped. The potential to harness the untapped energy was further explored through a comprehensive study involving the integration of Hydrogen Energy storage into DC microgrids.

articleTitle: Light Load Efficiency Improvement of Flying Capacitor-type Current-Fed DAB Converter for 1500V DC-grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a three-level current-fed dual active bridge (DAB) converter to achieve a wide high-efficiency range for DC voltage and load variation. The proposed control provides zero voltage switching (ZVS) by triangular current mode (TCM) under a wide DC voltage range. Additionally, the transformer root mean square (RMS) current is drastically reduced compared with the conventional control because the DC-voltage ratio is regulated by voltage control to match with the transformer turn ratio. Moreover, the proposed control improves the light load efficiency using the full-bridge (FB) and the half-bridge (HB) modes. The loss analysis results show that the proposed control reduces switching by 46%. The conduction losses were reduced by 53%. The proposed three-level current-fed DAB converter achieves an efficiency of 93.5% or higher over a wide voltage range from 160V to 320V. Finally, the experimental results indicated that the total loss is reduced by 63% at 0.2p.u.

articleTitle: Cabling Requirements for Low-Voltage DC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In the past years Low-Voltage Direct Current (LVDC) microgrids have gained interest for various reasons. Many aspects have been studied, such as energy efficiency, stability, control strategies, etc. However, when it comes to cable design, the bread and butter still comes from traditional Alternating Current (AC) systems. This paper analyses the effect of cable parameters on both system stability and short-circuit protection to derive guidelines for LVDC specific cable design. System stability does not impose limitations on the cable design, however selective protection does. This paper concludes that an LVDC cable should have an inductance value as low as possible, with no specific needs for a low cable capacitance, as is desired in AC systems.

articleTitle: Conceptual Verification of AC and DC Hybrid Interconnection System for Decentralized DC Microgrids with Flexible Power Supply Configuration Using Multi Level Virtual Conductor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This research verifies the concept of a decentralized hybrid power conditioner that is interconnected to the conventional AC commercial grid and performs bidirectional power supply/demand coordination through the additional household DC distribution network. It is expected to realize a disaster-resistant and highly operational power infrastructure by enabling free placement of renewable energy and bidirectional power distribution among households using an additional DC bus. Conceptual simulation results confirmed that the decentralized interconnection system can supply power from power sources in the DC grid to the conventional AC load while preventing reverse power flow to the AC commercial grid. It was also shown that this system can operate as an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) against AC grid blackout, and it was possible to compensate for a power shortage in one household from the power sources of another household via DC bus without any communication among sources. Furthermore, it was confirmed that the reverse power flow prevention was realized through a prototype experiment.

articleTitle: Control of Interlinking Converters for DC Multi-Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the control design of interlinking converters in DC multi-microgrids. We present a passivity framework and use this to propose a solution where each ILC satisfies an appropriate passivity condition which leads to stability and scalability of the DC multi-microgrids under reasonable assumptions. We illustrate the practicality of our approach with two examples of various DC-DC converters suitable for interlinking conversion.

articleTitle: Isolated Bidirectional DC/DC Converter for LVDC Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes an isolated bidirectional DC/DC converter designed for LVDC grid with bipolar output. A dual active bridge (DAB) converter has been widely studied and applied for isolated bidirectional DC/DC converter, although limitation of input and output voltage range. In order to overcome the weakness of a DAB converter, the proposed converter is composed of an input series output series (ISOS) buck-boost converter and a DAB converter. The ISOS buck-boost converter is formed by connecting buck-boost converters in series with the wide input and output voltage range. The DAB converter, which consists of a 3-level neutral point clamp (NPC) topology and a transformer for isolation, is responsible for bidirectional power control. The bipolar voltage outputs are provided using isolated and series connected two outputs, enabling independent power control. In this paper, the performance and feasibility of the proposed converter are experimentally verified through hardware implementation.

articleTitle: A Design of Solar Power Recharged Lead Carbon Battery System for a 3-Meter Tender
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Based on a review of solar rechargers for a lead-acid battery, this paper presents a lead-carbon battery solar power recharger for a 3-meter tender. A real-time indication of the maximum capacity of the lead-carbon battery is designed, and a peak performance capability is built in to provide the lead-carbon battery chemically ages. Experimental tests are reviewed to support this novel design.

articleTitle: A Unified Notation for Load Flow Formulation in AC/DC Power Grids with Flexible Power Topology Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for obtaining a unified notation of load flow formulation in alternating current/direct current (AC/DC) power grids while accommodating the flexibility of power topology variations. With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources and development of smart grid technologies, power systems are becoming more complex and interconnected, incorporating both AC and DC application. Therefore, we propose a unified notation that can seamlessly handle both AC and DC power flows while allowing for variations in power topology. The proposed notation offers a comprehensive framework for load flow calculations, enabling load flow optimisation and analysis in power grid design.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling and Analysis of DC Space Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This work presents a space microgrid architecture for long-term space exploration and human presence in space. It also considers internal and external microgrid faults, and their effects on the functionality of the space habitat. Additionally, it presents a qualitative reliability assessment model for the space microgrid based on Fault Tree Analysis (FTA). The paper presents different failure modes of the power system components, classifies their importance, and assesses the reliability of the system in multiple phases of operation and with different power management and control systems. Simulation results to assess the microgrid's reliability for various disturbance scenarios in a space habitat model are shown.

articleTitle: Arc Characteristics in Multiple Pole DC Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Due to the absence of zero crossings in a DC current compared to an AC current, DC arc extinguishing is difficult in DC circuit breakers (DCCB). To overcome this difficulty of arc extinguishing, DC circuit breakers are frequently designed and built by series connecting multiple poles of a 3 phase AC circuit breaker. During the mechanical contact opening, the fault current of the DC circuit gradually reduces as the arc path resistance increases with time. The arc can be extinguished quickly if the arc path resistance can be increased quickly. By increasing the series connected switches, the arc path resistance can be increased. This paper presents the arc characteristics of a multiple pole DC circuit breaker based on analytical and experimental approaches.

articleTitle: End-to-End Direct Current Power Networks as Enabler of Sustainable Green Electric Power for All
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The inadequacy of transmitting ultra-low-cost green sustainable power generation from photovoltaics is a major issue. Implementing an end-to-end high voltage direct current macrogrid is a potential solution. Leveraging the medium-voltage direct current distribution and high-voltage direct current transmission interconnects are necessary for newer utility-scale photovoltaics plants. To achieve this, a low-loss end-to-end direct current network design is proposed in this paper. Need for power electronic based modular converters and intelligent power flow control techniques are also emphasized for realization of proposed design. Significant power savings resulting into low-cost of electrical power can be achieved using such an end-to-end design for direct current power networks.

articleTitle: Device Providing DC Short-Circuit Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This work introduces a short-circuit current device (SCCD) for low voltage DC grids. This device aims to provide a fault current for protection devices which require an overcurrent for a rather long period in order to trip, e.g. melting fuses, in grid installations where such currents are usually not available because of converter current limits and smaller grid-side capacitors.

articleTitle: Novel DC-Link Voltage Balancing Control for 6.6kW Three-Port Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In the next few decades, electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure will play a crucial role in decarbonization. This paper discusses a three-port energy system (TPES), which can provide a flexible charging infrastructure for future EVs and smart grids. In TPES, photovoltaic (PV) arrays and EVs are interfaced with an electrical grid. In TPES, resonant and switched DC-DC converters are cascaded with full H-bridges via a DC-link. The problem with TPES is that harmonic disturbances cause double-line frequency ripples. In order to address this issue, bulky DC-link capacitors are used. Larger capacitors prevent high power density and system reliability. To address this issue, an active power decoupling control based on sinusoidal charging/discharging techniques is proposed. To absorb double-line frequency ripple power, it is imperative to consider the EV battery. Thus, the DC-link capacitor size can be substantially reduced, resulting in improved grid power quality. Finally, a 6.6kW single-phase TPES prototype is tested to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control strategies.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of a Four Level Quasi Nested Converter in 3-Phase 4-Wire Microgrid Islanded Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In this work, a Model Predictive Control (MPC strategy) is introduced for its application in a four-level quasinested topology, supplying three-phase loads on islanded microgrids. Additionally, a Hysteresis Multiband Control (HMB) is proposed to mitigate the fourth-wire neutral current. The proposed control strategy is capable to synthesize the required output space vectors to ensure perfect tracking of load currents under different loading conditions, while also ensuring voltage balance between the dc-link capacitors. The proposed converter topology is based on a reduced number of components compared to other mature converter topologies, such as the neutral-point clamped converter (NPC) or the active neutral-point clamped converter (ANPC) topologies, when compared in terms of the number of output voltage levels, since this quasi-nested topology does not require passive clamping devices such as diodes or active switches. Moreover, no floating dc-link capacitors with asymmetrical voltage levels are employed, thus simplifying the dc-link capacitor voltage balance mechanism. This work presents the switching operation principles, MPC control, and HMB control law when supplying an unbalanced three-phase fourwire RL load. Control law formulation and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Model Development of Commercial Ferroelectric Class 2 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This article explains the adaptation of a dipole polarization model to describe the DC voltage and frequency dependence of MLCCs. To demonstrate the practical suitability of the model, it will be tested using measurements on selected MLCCs from Wüirth Elektronik's portfolio. The number of fitting parameters is reduced, allowing an efficient fitting of an extensive capacitor portfolio. The model is developed for implementation in simulating software such as Spice.

articleTitle: A Novel DC Circuit Breaker with an Absorbing Branch Based on TVS Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Circuit breakers used in DC applications depend on energy absorbing elements to dissipate the energy generated during the interruption process. These elements, frequently presenting a non-linear voltage-current characteristic, allow the absorption of high amounts of energy. Commonly applied energy absorbing elements consist of Metal Oxide Varistors (MOVs) thanks to their low cost and good overvoltage suppression capacity. On the other hand, MOVs have low operating speed and may experience thermal runaway. To address MOVs shortcomings, this paper proposes a hybrid circuit breaker with a Transient Voltage Suppressor (TVS) diode as an alternative to the MOV. Design guidelines for a proper selection of TVS devices are provided.

articleTitle: The Effect of Voltage Dips on Home Appliances During DC Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This study examines the effect of voltage dips on the operation of home appliances connected to a DC power supplies. The results show that the effect of voltage dips in DC voltage on home appliances depends on the depth and duration of the dips.

articleTitle: Fast Breaking of Currents in Applications up to 800 V DC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The increasing use of DC systems in many different fields requires switching and protecting devices that are developed and optimized for the respective task. A common trait of such applications is the power electronics-based supply of those grids, which severely limits the available short-circuit current and therefore calls for short detection and interruption times of faults. However, as most devices in these applications also contain capacitive filters or DC link storages, there must be a control of the inrush current to avoid nuisance tripping and to ensure selectivity. A more and more common voltage range for the considered grids, e.g., in telecommunications or industrial production sites, is above 400 V up to 800 V [1] [2]. This work therefore evaluates the switching behavior of currently available switching devices subjected to DC voltages of up to 220 V. Based on those results, a novel switching concept is designed and validated. The initial goal is to achieve a switching capacity of at least 400 V and going up to 800 V per single pole in the common device width of 17.5 mm (with DIN-rail mounting) [3] by means of an externally excited magnetic field.

articleTitle: A Design Review of a Pure Solar-Power Supply for Surveillance Farming Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents a review of a Solar-powered DC Supply in the processing of a minimalist design for a Surveillance Farming Robot, which monitors the animals at the farm. The rechargeable battery in this Solar-powered DC Supply is recharged while the robot moves around the farm on a sunny day. This Autonomous robot can be online remotely controlled and monitored by farmers. Solar DC supplies have been operated to support the robot while the robot is constantly being tested and improved in 5 years. The experiments conclude the Solar-powered DC Supply is able to stand alone to support a minimalist design of a Surveillance Farming Robot.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Simple Low-Cost and Real-Time Solar Power Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Because of cheap conversion technology, zero green-house-gas (GHG) emission, and abundant availability almost everywhere, solar energy is contended to be a cost-effective alternate source of energy. It has the potential to meet ever-increasing energy demands while mitigating the environmental concerns associated with fossil fuels. As solar energy is intermittent in nature, the design of a reliable and cost-effective system requires site-specific weather information. A real-time and low-cost portable solar power monitoring system is a realistic solution for the assessment of energy generation at any site. Real-time site-specific solar power generation data for existing weather conditions is also important for the cyber physical representation of a solar photovoltaic system known as digital twin. In these contexts, a simple real-time and low-cost solar power monitoring system is proposed, implemented, and tested in this paper. The system is designed using a low-cost edge computing device, a Raspberry Pi, a voltage sensor, a current sensor, and the measured data is monitored through the Thing Speak<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> cloud platform. Test results of the system, which consists of two 5W photovoltaic modules, show its potential to be used in assessing site specific power generation capacity, PV plant performance monitoring, and in developing a digital twin of a PV system.

articleTitle: A Review of Solar DC Microgrids Design for Smart Farming in a New Zealand Lifestyle Block
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents a review of Solar DC Microgrids design energizing a small farm where irrigation is operated for a commercial cut-flower shade house and realtime animal control units. The irrigation unit has small-size DC Microgrids providing daily water pumping and irrigation under realtime online monitoring and remote control. An image-processing design enables power management to optimize the use of resources. The system irrigates 600 pots of Hydrangeas in a 2000 Square Meters shade house using a 100W solar panel and 20Ah battery. These Solar DC Microgrids are also designed to support animal control units, including water and fencing control. Such Solar DC Microgrids have been operated at low cost for 6 years.

articleTitle: Extending Supercapacitor Assisted Loss Management Approach for Efficiency Improvements in Solar Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Renewable energy inverters have several loss components, such as static losses and high frequency switching losses in semiconductors; transformer losses such as copper and core components; and input capacitor losses. For a given power output and an input DC voltage, these losses depend on transistor parameters and transformer specifications in addition to the, voltage stress, rms current in each element. This paper discusses an extension of supercapacitor assisted loss management technique (SCALoM) to reduce the typical losses in solar inverters. Proposed SCA(Supercapacitor assisted)-technique reduces the voltage stress and rms current in the internal components of the inverters. An extensive analysis of the impact of the proposed technique on the power loss components of solar inverters has been carried out in this paper. SCA-inverter arrangement makes it possible to operate the inverters with higher valued voltage sources than their input voltage range and the preliminary experimental implementation and validation of the proposed SCA-inverter technique shows significant efficiency improvement.

articleTitle: Topology Design and Analysis of Bidirectional Battery DC-DC Converter for DC Grid Voltage Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of Dual Active Bridge (DAB), CLLLC resonant circuit, and CLLC resonant circuit topologies applied as bidirectional battery DC/DC converters for the DC bus voltage control in the low-voltage and low-power DC microgrid application. The circuit design process starts with the high-frequency transformer design (HFT) for the DAB and CLLLC converters. All DC/DC converter designs are optimized to maximize the phase shift control variable resolution in the rated power range through the circuit parameter iterative adjustment based on the converter circuit simulation results. The CLLC converter parameters are derived from optimized CLLLC parameters with its HFT redesigned to meet the turns ratio and the modified magnetization inductance requirement. The secondary side compensation capacitor ratio of the CLLC resonant circuit is adjusted iteratively based on circuit simulation results to maximize the phase shift control variable resolution in the rated power range. The PLECS circuit simulation is constructed to compare and evaluate the voltage and current waveforms of the converters and transformers, the power loss, and the efficiency of different circuit topologies. The proposed method is applied to identify the best battery DC/DC converter topology for a 4 kW 100 V DC microgrid with a 4 kW PMAC generator connected as an AC power source. The circuit simulation results validate that the CLLLC resonant converter has the best efficiency over a wide power range in the full battery voltage range.

articleTitle: Protection and Control Strategy for Battery Energy Storage System in Islanded LV DC Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The utilization and integration of renewable energy sources (RES), called distributed energy resources (DERs), have advanced significantly within the framework of power system design, especially in a microgrid. Some of RESs like photovoltaic (PV), wind, waves, and tides are naturally intermittent. Therefore, battery energy storage system (BESS) is needed in the microgrid system to minimize power fluctuations and improve power quality. In this paper, protection and control strategy for BESS in DC microgrid are presented. First, the protection of BESS by coordinating the current-time curve of each BESS protection device is presented. Protection devices are modelled by using a solid-state DC circuit breaker. Then, a droop control method with voltage restoration is implemented in BESS to maintain the DC microgrid bus voltage at 500 Vdc. Finally, the simulation results verify that the proposed protection coordination with droop control and voltage restoration works robustly by maintaining constant DC bus voltage despite the fluctuation of the load. This paper focuses on the protection and control of BESS in the LV DC microgrid.

articleTitle: Design of an Efficient Energy Harvesting System for Smart Grid Connection Based on Piezoelectric Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The production of electrical energy is now a crucial component of the power system due to the rising demand brought on by population expansion and economic development. Experts are looking for new and more sustainable energy sources to meet the rising demand. One of the most promising methods in the sector is the application of piezoelectric material to transform environmental vibrations into electrical energy. The proposed study focuses on the design, optimization, and experimental validation of an effective piezoelectric-based energy-harvesting prototype that serves as the foundation for the development of a modular piezoelectric system to capture the kinetic energy of moving people and traffic for integration and connection with smart grids. In this study, four different configurations of two types of piezoelectric materials were examined and compared in both simulation and experimental tests. The four examined configurations are: series connection, parallel connection, series-parallel connection and parallel-series connection. Two different prototypes are implemented, which include eight piezoelectric elements. The amount of stored energy produced by both prototypes demonstrates how effective the parallel-series configuration is in terms of simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Availability Analysis of Industrial DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Direct Current (DC) microgrids have gained significant interest over the past years. Especially in industry where, the benefits are plentiful. Benefits such as efficiency gains, CAPEX reduction, but most definitely also resilience against Alternating Current (AC) side disturbances and power quality issues. This paper presents a method using a semi-Markov model to quantitatively compare the instantaneous and steady state availability of an industrial DC distribution to a conventional industrial AC distribution. Three different scenarios are presented for which either the instantaneous or the steady state availability is determined. As expected, the DC microgrid proves to be more available than the conventional AC distribution. This paper demonstrates an increase of over an order of magnitude, while also considering converter failure.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Different Operational Strategies for DC Links in Medium-Voltage Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The demand for grid expansion in medium-voltage grids is expected to increase due to the growing penetration of decentralized generation plants and new types of power consumers. In addition to the conventional expansion of medium-voltage grids, an alternative expansion with DC links is possible, which provides additional flexibility through an active and reactive power flow control capability. During the planning and operation of these DC links, suitable operational strategies are required to determine optimized set points for the corresponding AC/DC converters. In this paper, different operational strategies of DC links in medium-voltage grids are investigated by different formulations of an optimal power flow problem. For this purpose, technical aspects such as current and voltage limits as well as grid losses are investigated.

articleTitle: A Fully Distributed Electrical Power System for Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel fully distributed electri-cal power system (FD-EPS) for small satellites. Current EPSs are first summarized, and satellite energy balance and requirements for EPS are analyzed. The design of a FD-EPS, which divides each function in the current EPS into parallelizable modules, is then proposed. Each module can operate independently or be controlled by an on-board computer. The modules are connected through a power bus and a communication bus to simplify the connection. The capability of the EPS can be expanded by adding more modules or improving the modules' capability. Prototypes for each module type were developed, and preliminary tests were conducted.

articleTitle: Dual-Channel Isolated Gate Driver Power Supply Based on Ultrasonic Power Transmission Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Power electronic converters are the key devices of DC microgrids, which makes the power system highly efficient and reliable to access distributed generations and loads. The power semiconductor devices used in the converter demand gate drivers with high voltage withstanding capability and good anti-electromagnetic interference performance. An isolated gate driver to meet these challenging requirements is presented in this article. A novel isolated gate driver power supply using ultrasonic power transmission technology with a symmetrical acoustic transmission structure for dual-channel synchronous output is proposed. The transmitter piezoelectric ceramic of the ultrasonic power transmission system along with its transmitter circuit have been epoxy encapsulated to achieve a very high breakdown voltage. The experimental results are obtained from a gate driver application platform to demonstrate the validity of the proposed isolated gate driver power supply.

articleTitle: Comparison of Energy Consumption of an Inverter-Driven Refrigerator Under DC Operation vs AC Operation – Preliminary Investigation on DC Operability of Whiteware
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Energy-efficient whiteware will reduce the power consumption of a household. Reducing the number of power converter stages within a whiteware helps to enhance the efficiency of the system. Modern commercially available inverter-driven whiteware such as a refrigerator, operates internally on a DC bus, allowing direct powering from the DC bus of a renewable energy system. However, the use of an energy storage system is mandatory to buffer the fluctuating nature of renewable energy. This paper presents the comparison of power consumption of a household inverter-driven refrigerator operating from the traditional AC supply, versus a DC supply based on the removal of the front-end rectifier. The refrigerator was also tested for its wider DC operating voltage range so that a supercapacitor module could be used to buffer the fluctuating nature of renewable energy.

articleTitle: An Experimental Test Model for an Electric DC Power Boat Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental test model for DC power input to an electric boat reaching a desired speed to provide a theoretical understanding of DC electric power-driven propulsion, which is the replacement of combustion engines. This paper recommended a parameter “power coefficient” for electric boat design as an important indicator. While traveling at a desired speed and the power supply voltage is stable, the motor drive current is a key parameter to achieve the best power coefficient. Such a parameter can be realtime monitoring according to the natural properties of the DC powertrain in electric boats.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on Conducted EMI Characteristics of AC Home Appliances in DC Power Feed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The power supply of recent home appliances comprises a rectifier and switching converter. In this study, the conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) of AC home appliances in DC power feeds was investigated to verify the applicability of currently marketed products to DC microgrids. Results showed that if the DC bus voltage is set to around 320–340 Vdc, many appliances can be safely used for meeting EMC regulations without any modification of the internal circuit configuration. DC-fed appliances without rectification operation were identified to have lower noise levels than that for AC power fed, particularly in the kHz band. The measurement results suggest that when home appliances are fed DC power, they satisfy the international standards for conducted emission.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Production Machine's Energy Efficiency in the Transformation Process From AC To DC Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Industry is one of the largest producers of greenhouse gases. In order to meet international climate targets, there is increasing pressure on industry to reduce climate-damaging emissions by cutting energy consumption. Increasing the energy efficiency of electrical grids and manufacturing machinery can make a significant contribution to reducing energy consumption. DC microgrids represent a promising approach to increasing energy efficiency in the manufacturing environment. Establishing this new form of grid requires the availability of DC grid-compatible machines. These are still rare, so converting conventional AC machines for DC grids is gaining increasing interest. This paper describes the conversion of an ordinary AC-supplied injection molding machine for operation in an industrial DC grid. The focus is on the conversion's influence on the machine's efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Controllers for Offshore DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: DC microgrids (MGs) are emerging as an appealing option for the supply of reliable and efficient power to offshore industries because of their capacity to incorporate a variety of distributed energy resources (DERs). This is possible due to the advancements in power electronics technology, which play a fundamental role in enabling the operation of DC MGs. Crucially, the effective functioning of each power converter in a DC MG relies on a well-designed controller that can maintain DC voltages within specified limits. Furthermore, the controller ensures the system's reliability and stability in the event of any disturbances. However, designing an effective control system for DC MGs poses significant challenges, owing to the inherent variability and intermittent nature of many DERs and load variations. Hence, a suitable and well-tuned controller for each power converter is required to ensure stable and reliable operation. In this paper, a comparative study of four control schemes proposed for DC MGs is presented: Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) voltage-mode control, PID-based cascaded control, cascaded average current-mode (ACM) control, and sliding mode control (SMC). The performance parameters of each controller are assessed through the electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation. The SMC approach has been identified as the most suitable control strategy to use for the DC MG model.

articleTitle: Modelling and Design of a Droop-Based Cascaded Controller for LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: This paper proposes a digital cascaded control strategy for integrating an LLC resonant converter into a DC Microgrid. The designed control scheme is particularly suitable for battery storage applications in discharging mode. The outer loop of the cascaded controller is a droop controller which provides the reference current according to the DC grid voltage. The inner loop regulates the current according to the reference by pulse frequency modulation (PFM). A seventh-order state-space model based on first harmonic approximation (FHA) and extended describing function (EDF) was built to assist the controller design. The proposed control scheme is validated for both buck and boost operation mode in the PLECS simulation environment.

articleTitle: EV Internal Charging and Grid-to-Battery Efficiency: An Empirical Study Based on Selected EV and EVSE Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Supporting the 2015 Paris Agreement on rapid decarbonisation of all economic sectors to limit global warming to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.5^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$</tex> above pre-industrial levels, Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ) has committed transitioning to net-zero with the opportunity of reaching a more productive, sustainable and inclusive economy. With a 2030 target of 100% renewable electricity, and 2050 target of carbon-neutral economy, the NZ government has mandated adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) to reduce 39% of domestic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}\ \mathrm{e}$</tex> missions arising from the transport sector. This paper presents internal efficiency measurements of some of the typical EVs used in NZ with emphasis on maximum charge power transfer against selected AC and DC fast chargers. An efficiency summary of eight electric vehicle supply equipments (EVSEs) adopted within NZ infrastructure is also included in this manuscript to showcase charging performances under various EV loads. Active battery thermal management systems of EVs under study are investigated based on internal charge profiles recorded by power quality meters and OBD2 data (EVSE power vs EV battery power). Overall, it is revealed that the ultimate grid-to-battery efficiency varies from 85% to 92.6%, with significant energy being consumed by the vehicle BMS for battery thermal management.

articleTitle: Experimental Assessment of LVDC-Grid Stability Optimization using Circuit Simulation and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Low-voltage direct current networks play a central role in the realization of a sustainable, resilient energy supply. The stabilization of the networks during design and operation of the grids is a particular challenge since more and more components must be included in the stability analysis and control. Therefore, it is desirable to increasingly apply automated computations and artificial intelligence techniques for stability optimization. This paper describes the investigations for the experimental validation of a new approach for stability optimization, which can be applied in regular grid operation. A direct current network is mapped into a digital twin for automated computation of stability states. A classification model establishes the relationship between the network input parameters and the stability states, so that improved network parameter settings can be determined with a novel optimization method. A novel impedance measurement based on pseudorandom binary sequences (PRBS) enables precise characterization of grid components and continuous stability monitoring. Following the component characterization, the digital twin model is transferred and validated on a direct current network testbed and at the example of adjusting characteristic droop control curves.

articleTitle: Use-Case- Dependent Modeling Approach for Computer Simulation of Hybrid AC-DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: An analysis-use-case dependent modeling approach for the computer simulation of hybrid AC-DC grids employing component models with varying degrees of complexity is presented. Three different component model complexity levels for three different component functionality groups and three different use cases are defined. The component modeling is based on analytical averaged descriptions of the converter behavior and introduces a standardized model interface. The proposed merits of this approach are faster simulation times and easier result evaluation making this approach suitable for automated grid simulation and assisted layout evaluation. This makes a technical and economical design evaluation of AC- DC grids much more feasible. Furthermore, manufacturers of grid components could use this design approach to develop models with unified interface ports to be used in DC grid model component libraries. The optimization of computing time for different simulation run times is tested and presented using a simulation tool developed using this approach.

articleTitle: Combined Planning of LVDC and MVDC Grids for Public Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Based on the large technological developments in the field of power electronic devices and DC technology, not only DC microgrids but also DC distribution grids for public power supply gain practical relevance. In this course, DC infrastructure promises to overcome some future challenges on MV and LV level. For the planning of MVDC and LVDC distribution grids, meta-heuristic optimization techniques have recently been applied in order to efficiently design either the LV or the MV level. However, an important aspect of the planning of novel DC grids is the combined optimization of LVDC and MVDC level in order to leverage economic potential. In this paper, a comprehensive planning framework for the combined LVDC and MVDC grid planning is presented. After providing a theoretical foundation for the DC grid planning task, the combined planning framework is presented. A hierarchical structure-dependent methodology has been developed deriving technically and economically optimized LVDC and MVDC distribution grids. The planning framework is applied within a case study on two supply areas: A rural and an urban region. The results show a significant reduction of cable trench lengths and costs when an incentive is set.

articleTitle: Ambient Environmental Energy Harvesting for Supercapacitor Driven Battery-less IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: The research project centres on developing a robust energy harvesting system for IoT devices, emphasizing the potential of green energy technologies. Current findings underscore the dominance of solar panels, highlighting their superior power generation compared to thermoelectric generators and Piezoelectric harvesters. Supercapacitors emerge as effective energy storage, replacing batteries and ensuring consistent power supply to IoT devices during energy harvesting fluctuations. Challenges include optimizing thermal and vibration harvesters, and refining the power management module. Future work aims at reducing component inefficiencies, implementing an advanced control system, and integrating smart sensors for dynamic environmental adaptation. These efforts anticipate elevating the efficiency and sustainability of IoT devices reliant on green energy harvesting technologies.

articleTitle: Incremental Conductance MPPT Optimization System Modeling using PID Control with Fuzzy Gain Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Solar irradiation fluctuations can shift the PV module's operating point away from its maximum power point (MPP). To maintain the MPP, the widely used incremental conductance (IC) method is employed as part of the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique for PV systems due to its simplicity. In this study, authors enhance the MPPT IC method by integrating a PID control scheme with fuzzy gain scheduling (FGS). Using simulations in Simulink with irradiation variations between 800-1000-800 W/m2, this study observes that the MPPT IC-PID system with FGS outperforms the conventional MPPT IC system. It significantly reduces steady-state oscillations from 5.79% to just 0.22% and shortens the average response time from 12.15ms to 1.06ms. These improvements result in increased energy production (up to 23.36 Ws) and reduced tracking error (by up to 1.05%), compared to the conventional MPPT IC system's 2.297 Ws and 9.43% tracking error.

articleTitle: Problem Definition of Modelling and Simulation of Industrial DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: In recent years, industrial direct current (DC) microgrids have become more popular in Germany, but the transfer from science to the field is still lacking. For electrical planners who have to plan and conceptualize the DC microgrid for industrial companies, a general planning procedure for industrial DC grids does not exist yet. For industrial companies, questions arise about personal and equipment safety, stability, and flexibility options. For many of the issues, there are no userfriendly methods for the electrical specialist planner and the industrial customer. This paper presents problems from science and practice in the planning, dimensioning, and operation of industrial DC microgrids. The focus is on experiences from the practical application of DC microgrids. The open problems from practice can be divided into problems in the operation scenarios of regular operation, fault scenarios, selectivity, and control evaluation. Until user-friendly methods can be provided for electrical designers, simulation of DC grids can fill the gap. Finally, a way to solve some of the problems through ontologybased modelling and simulation is presented.

articleTitle: Impact of Thermal Energy Storage on Optimal Sizing of a Grid Connected Wind-Photovoltaic-Battery System for an Industry Edged Community
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: New Zealand is committed to decarbonize its energy sector by 2050, and from the perspectives of greenhouse gas emissions, and efficiency in generation, transmission and distribution, electricity is the energy source of choice. To meet the significant increasing demand for electricity, solar photovoltaic and wind turbine generators have the potential to offer cost-effective and environmentally friendly solutions. Solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine generator (WTG) have the potential to offer a cost-effective and environmentally friendly solution. Energy storage systems (ESS) such as battery (BT), capacitor (CAP), pumped-hydro energy storage (PHES) and thermal energy storage (TES) are commonly integrated with these renewable energy sources (RESs) to overcome their intermittency and non-dispatchability. An optimal combination of renewable energy sources (RESs), ESSs, their operation and control along with load flexibility can enhance the cost-effectiveness and reliability of a system. The impact of on-site TES on total system cost and excess energy generation of a grid connected PV-WTG-ESS system for different renewable fraction (RF) is investigated. The electrical demand of a meat-factory and its edged community is considered in optimal sizing of the system. The demand of a meat-factory is mainly composed of its thermal load, electrical load and the charging of electric freights transports, whereas the community load used here comprises the household appliances of 3000 houses and their belonging electric vehicles. Half of both the EVs and freight transport are charged at night and the rest are charged during the day. The optimal sizing of different elements for given renewable fractions (RF) is performed using a Genetic Algorithm (GA). The result suggests that integration of TES provides enhanced flexibility to RESs and thus reduces the generation of excess energy and total cost of a HRES significantly. The sharing of on-site generation from RESs in a meat factory to its edged residential community improves cost-effectiveness and enhances the reliability of a HRES.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) Electrolyser-Fuel Cell Setup Using Simulink Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Fifth International Conference on DC Microgrids (ICDCM)
abstract: Hydrogen as an energy carrier is becoming more and more advanced and attractive with the global trend of achieving a net zero emissions policy. So, with the developments in renewable energy systems around the world, hydrogen-related devices like electrolysers, fuel cells, and hydrogen microturbines are commonly integrated into the power system. This work presents a study on the mathematical modelling of a PEM electrolyser and equivalent electrical circuit modelling of a PEM fuel cell. The PEM fuel cell model is tested with a standard load profile which simulates the dynamic behaviour of a practical fuel cell. Vital parameters of the PEM electrolyser namely hydrogen production rate, efficiency, and cell voltage behave as functions of input current, temperature, and pressure of the system. The behaviour of these parameters considering variations of two input parameters simultaneously, is investigated in an analytical study.
